tools.name: list_mailboxes

title.en: List mail folders and count unread mail

tools.description: Lists the mail folders of one or all accounts with their role (inbox, sent, drafts, trash, junk, archive) and the number of unread and of all messages in each, read from the mail server now. Use it to answer how many unread mails there are. An account that cannot be reached answers from the cache and is named in errors.

account.description: Account id from list_accounts; every account when omitted.

Habe ich neue Mails?

Wie viele Mails liegen im Posteingang?

Do I have new mail?
Which folders are in my mailbox?
How many mails are in my inbox?

tools.name: get_message
tools.description: Returns one mail: sender, recipients, subject, date, whether it is unread or flagged, its text (at most 12000 characters, truncated says if it was cut) and its attachments. Reading does not mark the mail as read. Take the id from find_messages.

tools.name: mark_messages

title.de: Mails als gelesen oder markiert setzen
title.en: Mark mails as read or flagged

tools.description: Marks up to 100 mails as read or unread and/or as flagged or not flagged. Answers per mail which were changed and which failed with a reason.

read.description: true marks the mails as read, false as unread.

flagged.description: true flags the mails, false removes the flag.

tools.name: move_messages
tools.description: Moves up to 100 mails to a folder of their own account, named by role (inbox, sent, drafts, trash, junk, archive) or by folder name. A mail already in the target counts as done. Answers per mail which were moved and which failed with a reason.

to.description: A mailbox role or the name of a folder.

Leg die Belege in den Ordner Steuer
Schieb die Newsletter in den Papierkorb
Sortier die Mail von Anna in den Ordner Arbeit

Put the receipts into the Steuer folder

File the mail from Anna into the Work folder

tools.name: create_draft
tools.description: Stores a new mail, a reply or a forward as a draft in the drafts folder of an account. It never sends. With replyTo (a message id) the recipient, subject, thread and the quoted original are taken from that message; to, cc and subject override them. Attachments of the original are not carried over. Returns the draft id and what the draft says (to lists every recipient, cc included); send_mail sends it.

body.description: What you write; the quoted original follows it.

replyTo.description: The id of the message to answer or forward.

Entwirf eine Mail an ben@example.org wegen der Rechnung
Leite die Mail mit dem Vertrag an meine Kollegin weiter

Forward the mail with the contract to my colleague

tools.name: list_accounts
tools.description: Lists the mail accounts set up in haex-mail (id, display name, address) and, under importable, the password manager entries tagged for haex-mail that could become an account (id, title, user name). Never returns a password or server credentials. Start here when the user wants to set up a mail account: importable shows whether a saved login can be used.

tools.name: import_account

title.en: Import a mail account from the password manager

tools.description: Turns a password manager entry tagged for haex-mail into a mail account. The entry must hold the mail server settings. Take the entry id from the importable list of list_accounts. The password is read by haex-mail itself and never passes through the agent.

passwordItemId.description: The entry id from list_accounts, importable.

Mach aus dem Eintrag Arbeit ein Mailkonto
Importiere das vorhandene Mailkonto aus dem Passwort-Tresor

Set up the account from the password manager in haex-mail
Make the entry Work a mail account
Import the existing mail account from the password vault

tools.name: open_account_setup

title.en: Prepare the setup of a mail account

tools.description: Prepares the new mail account form in haex-mail with the given address and server settings. It has no password field: the user opens the haex-mail window and types the password into the form themselves. Use it when no saved login can be imported.

tools.name: list_rules
tools.description: Lists the mail rules of haex-mail: id, name, account, whether it is switched on, its conditions and actions, who created it (user or agent) and whether its target folder is gone.

Zeig mir meine Regeln in haex-mail

en: Which mail rules do I have?

tools.name: add_rule
tools.description: Creates a permanent mail rule: when a new inbox message meets ALL conditions, the actions run. Conditions: sender, recipient or subject contains a text, or the message has an attachment. Actions: move to a mailbox role (inbox excluded: sent, drafts, trash, junk, archive) or, for a rule on one account, to a folder name; mark as read; flag. There is no action that forwards or sends a message. Optionally runs once on the newest 1000 messages already in the inbox. The user is asked before every call.

name.description: A short name for the rule.

account.description: Account id from list_accounts; the rule covers every account when omitted.

contains.description: The text to look for, ignoring case; not used with attachment.

to.description: For move: a mailbox role (archive, trash, junk, sent, drafts) or, for one account, a folder name. A name that is a role name, in any case, always means the role, so a custom folder called like a role cannot be targeted.

applyToExisting.description: Also run the rule once on the existing inbox messages.

Erstelle eine Regel: Mails mit Anhang von Anna als gelesen markieren

tools.name: remove_rule
tools.description: Removes one mail rule by id or by name. When a name fits several rules nothing is removed and the ids are returned. Messages the rule already sorted stay where they are.

en: Delete the rule for shop.de

tools.name: find_messages
tools.description: Finds mails of one or all accounts in a folder (the inbox when omitted) by sender, recipient, subject, free text in the whole mailbox, date range, unread, flagged or attachment, searched on the server so older mails are found too. Newest first by default, one page at a time (at most 50). Returns ids to use with get_message, mark_messages, move_messages and delete_messages, plus total and hasMore. window says only the newest hits were looked at; fallback says the server refused the text and only sender, recipients and subject were checked.

account.description: Account id from list_accounts; every account when omitted.

mailbox.description: A mailbox role (inbox, sent, drafts, trash, junk, archive) or a folder name; the inbox when omitted.

unread.description: true for unread mails only, false for read ones only.

from.description: Part of the sender name or address.

to.description: Part of a recipient name or address.

text.description: Free text searched in the whole mailbox on the server.

descending.description: true (newest first, Z to A) when omitted.

limit.description: Page size, 25 when omitted, at most 50.

offset.description: Hits to skip, for the next page.

tools.name: create_mailbox
tools.description: Creates a new folder in one account. If the folder already exists nothing changes and created is false. Afterwards move_messages and find_messages can use it by name.

name.description: The folder name as the user writes it; a slash makes a subfolder on most servers.

tools.name: send_mail
tools.description: Sends a draft made with create_draft; this cannot be undone. The user is asked to agree to what the input says, so pass the draft exactly as create_draft returned it: draftId, to (every recipient, cc included), subject and body. If anything differs from the stored draft nothing is sent and the error names the draft's values. A copy goes to the sent folder and the draft is removed.

Schick die Antwort ab
Verschicke die Mail, die du vorbereitet hast
Versende den Entwurf jetzt
en: Send the draft to Anna
Send the reply now
Mail out the draft you prepared

tools.name: delete_messages
tools.description: Removes mails from the server for good, with no way back and not into the trash. To delete in the usual way use move_messages with the trash. The user is asked to agree, so pass each mail with its id and its exact subject; a mail whose subject differs on the server is not deleted. At most 100 mails. Answers per mail which were deleted and which failed with a reason.
